unresolved_added: Watermarks, QR blocks, Chinese publisher/footer material, Contents, references, and the AI-use report are not positive author-language evidence.
The intervention-strategy passage and the Notably introduction passage are explicitly disclosed as ChatGPT-assisted and must not seed human-style language rules.
ELA, annual tourist count, and hotel-tax revenue are narrow proxies for environmental, social, and economic conditions; construct validity is not established.
H, N, and T use different physical scales, yet the coupled terms and intervention vectors lack a complete dimensional analysis.
ELA change is attributed to tourist pressure and tax-funded restoration without a causal identification design or separation from climate drivers.
Tourist arrivals are treated as a logistic population although visitors are flows, seasonality is strong, and carrying capacity K is not independently justified.
The hotel-tax ODE does not explicitly include tax rates, lodging prices, collection lags, cruise visitors, or non-tourism revenue.
Policy effects omega_H, omega_N, and omega_T are added directly to state derivatives without documented units or a reproducible policy-to-coefficient mapping.
The 2013 Blob observation is removed and remaining years interpolated, but the exclusion rule, interpolation method, sensitivity, and retained sample size are not fully documented.
Nonlinear least squares is named without complete input data, starting values, bounds, residual diagnostics, confidence intervals, or holdout validation.
Figures 3, 4, and 8 show fitted behavior, but visual agreement is not a substitute for residual, predictive, and out-of-sample checks.
Nine allocation arrays do not establish coverage or optimality of the five-dimensional allocation simplex.
Eight policy vectors and the selected [-3,3,4] code lack a fully auditable mapping from integers to implementable policy magnitudes.
Allocation shares are optimized without a clearly frozen total budget, feasibility constraints, legal restrictions, or implementation costs.
The paper proposes iterative policy feedback but does not specify observation intervals, triggers, controller stability, delay, or rollback.
Several evaluation indicators reuse N and T, creating potential double counting that AHP weights do not remove.
Benefit and cost indicators are mixed; direction, clipping, and bounds are not consistently documented.
Equation (7) contains visually unstable arrows, exponents, and mu subscripts; its exact algebra must be checked against the source before reuse.
Equation (9) has unclear exponent signs and parameter placement, so the asserted normalization range is not independently established.
Equation (14) cannot be transcribed uniquely from the printed layout without inventing a numerator or exponent.
Equation (16) has a visually unclear fraction/equality continuation and may not produce the claimed score direction.
Equation (17) prints a minimum with zero, which appears inconsistent with a nonnegative waste amount unless a sign convention is supplied.
Equation (19) has unstable exponent notation and no empirical calibration of its threshold or slope.
The prose calls Equation (22) inverse exponential while the printed expression appears to be a power function.
Table 5 mixes fitted, substituted, and experience-based values without parameter-specific provenance and uncertainty.
The four judgment matrices are presented without named assessors, elicitation protocol, disagreement handling, or uncertainty.
Matrix consistency and aggregation evidence are not reported alongside the weights.
The final score scale and aggregation choices are not validated against observed resident, ecological, or economic outcomes.
The body reports a selected strategy score of 0.6894 while the Summary reports improvement to 0.692; rounding or pipeline differences are not reconciled.
The reported 0.446 baseline and model score changes have no external decision threshold or uncertainty interval.
Morris screening lacks a complete reproducible specification of parameter ranges, trajectories, levels, seed, and treatment of interactions.
Large local sensitivities such as r1=792.18 and k5=575.2 depend on parameter units and evaluation point, so raw magnitudes are not directly comparable.
Global Morris and local derivative rankings are described together without explaining differences in scale, range, or interpretation.
Cliff retreat is substituted for glacier ELA, changing the physical mechanism while retaining the same state-equation form.
The Big Sur transfer reuses structure and coefficients without a full recalibration table, comparative fit metrics, or held-out validation.
The change 0.32773 to 0.73563 is model-generated and should not be phrased as observed improvement.
The 15,000-visitors-per-day cap is not derived transparently from the displayed optimization or an enforceable capacity constraint.
The memo's 40-percent environmental allocation does not visibly match the selected vector [0.15,0.10,0.35,0.10,0.30].
The claim of up to 30-percent annual glacier-degradation reduction lacks a displayed derivation and uncertainty interval.
Housing affordability and tax relief are recommended without a housing-market model, incidence analysis, eligibility rule, or distributional assessment.
The paper itself excludes heatwaves, pandemics, and other unexpected events, limiting robustness of the proposed policy.
The paper itself acknowledges that immediate policy effects ignore implementation delay and may bias forecasts.
Source names are listed, but a frozen data bundle, exact URLs, retrieval dates, transformations, and licenses are not provided.
No complete code, environment, data bundle, parameter file, seed, or single replay command is supplied.
Single-paper observations may inform source-specific evidence only; they do not establish a general MCM writing or modeling rule.
